text:p.text:span: TMC New System: Structure and Development Technologies

draw:text-box.text:p: TMC Functional Modules
1. Master Data Maintenance and Upload Entry: users submit source matrix files, OTH data, and CRP data to establish the core input foundation for the workflow.
2. Preparation and Adjustment Layers: raw uploaded data is cleaned, standardized, and transformed into prepared and adjustment layers for downstream calculations.
3. Machine Line Split and Calculation: the system performs total market calculation, machine line split logic, and restatement processing to generate aligned market outputs.
4. Validation Layer: the TMC validation report is used to review data quality, trace anomalies, and verify whether calculated outputs are consistent with business rules.
Overall, each module supports a clear progression from data intake to calculation, correction, and final validation.
Development Technologies
Frontend: React, TypeScript, and Vite were used to build a responsive browser-based interface for upload, review, and reporting workflows.
Frontend deployment: the web interface is deployed on Vercel for fast delivery and easy iteration.
Backend: Python and FastAPI were used to implement APIs, business logic, and report generation functions.
Backend runtime: the backend service is deployed on Google Cloud Run using containerized delivery.
Database: PostgreSQL is used as the main relational database, hosted through Google Cloud SQL.
DevOps and deployment: Docker is used for containerization, Google Artifact Registry stores images, and GitHub Actions handles automatic deployment.
Cloud authentication: Workload Identity Federation with a GCP service account is used so GitHub Actions can deploy securely without long-lived static credentials.
Cross-origin and source control: CORS is configured for frontend-backend communication, and GitHub is used for source code management.
Deployment URL: https://thesis-rust-five.vercel.app/
GitHub repository: https://github.com/YanxiangDu2023/thesis
Main Database Tables
Upload tracking tables: upload_runs and planning_years record file upload history, processing status, and yearly data scope.
Master data tables: source_matrix_rows, reporter_list_rows, size_class_rows, brand_mapping_rows, group_country_rows, and machine_line_mapping_rows store reference mappings used by the workflow.
Input data tables: oth_data_rows, volvo_sale_data_rows, and tma_data_rows store the major uploaded business datasets.
Manual adjustment table: split_manual_rows stores manual split inputs and corrections for selected machine-line cases.
Report output tables: control_report_clean_runs/rows, crp_tma_report_runs/rows, crp_sal_report_runs/rows, and p00_report_runs/rows store generated report results and snapshots.
Process trace tables: report_run_history and excavators_split_case_runs/rows preserve run history, reusable snapshots, and auditability of intermediate outputs.
Frontend-Backend Interaction
1. The user performs actions in the React frontend, such as logging in, uploading files, running reports, or opening result pages.
2. The frontend sends HTTP requests to FastAPI endpoints on Cloud Run through the configured API base URL.
3. Authentication tokens and the site password are attached in request headers when protected APIs are called.
4. The backend validates access, processes business logic, reads or writes PostgreSQL data, and stores uploaded files when needed.
5. The backend returns structured JSON responses, which the frontend renders as tables, pipeline views, validation pages, and downloadable results.
This interaction model separates presentation logic from business logic while keeping the system modular and easier to maintain.
Deployment and CI/CD Process
1. Code changes are pushed to the main branch in GitHub.
2. GitHub Actions triggers the backend deployment workflow automatically when backend files are updated.
3. The workflow authenticates to Google Cloud through Workload Identity Federation rather than using a personal Google account directly.
4. Google Cloud verifies the GitHub workflow identity through the configured Workload Identity Provider and allows it to impersonate the deployment service account.
5. The backend Docker image is built and pushed to Google Artifact Registry.
6. The new image is then deployed to the Cloud Run service, which creates a new revision automatically.
This creates a secure and repeatable deployment pipeline linking GitHub, Artifact Registry, Cloud Run, and Cloud SQL.
Cloud Run Cost and Open Points
Cloud Run follows a pay-for-usage model, so cost depends on request count, execution time, CPU allocation, memory size, and egress traffic rather than a fixed server price.
This is suitable for the thesis system because backend workloads are irregular and can scale down when there is no active use.
Main cost-related components in the current architecture include Cloud Run, Cloud SQL, Artifact Registry storage, and network traffic.
For practical operation, cost can be reduced by keeping the service lightweight, limiting unnecessary revisions, and optimizing report execution time.
Open implementation point: the handling of validation and non-reporter brand logic is still being finalized and should be clarified in the next iteration of the system.
